claims.text: The starting material is an equiatomic Co20Cr20Fe20Ni20Ti20 elemental powder mixture.
Cast CoCrFeNiTi has low hardness and high porosity.
The proposed process uses approximately 6 hours of high-energy ball milling followed by SPS at 1000°C and 40 MPa for 10 minutes.
Approximately 6 hours of high-energy ball milling produces nanocrystalline grains smaller than 100 nm in CoCrFeNiTi.
Approximately 6 hours of milling produces high lattice strain in CoCrFeNiTi.
Milling-induced lattice strain lowers the activation-energy barrier for an FCC-to-BCC solid-solution transformation.
VEC governs FCC/BCC phase stability in high-entropy alloys, with intermediate VEC values favoring FCC/BCC coexistence.
A VEC range of approximately 7.5-8.0 promotes FCC/BCC coexistence.
Atomic-radius mismatch governs phase stability in the proposed CoCrFeNiTi FCC/BCC transition.
SPS at 1000°C facilitates near-theoretical densification of ball-milled CoCrFeNiTi.
SPS at 1000°C avoids excessive Ti-driven HCP precipitation.
Ti-driven HCP precipitation becomes thermodynamically favorable above approximately 1050°C.
SPS temperatures above 1050°C cause excessive grain growth or phase decomposition.
At least 6 hours of milling is required to generate sufficient lattice strain for the proposed phase transition.
The proposed process will produce a dual-phase FCC/BCC CoCrFeNiTi microstructure.
The processed alloy will reach at least 98% of theoretical density and less than 2% porosity.
The processed alloy will reach a Vickers hardness of at least 400 HV0.5.
Cast CoCrFeNiTi has a hardness of approximately 150-200 HV and porosity of 5-10%.
Cast CoCrFeNiTi is single-phase FCC or mixed FCC/BCC with coarse grains and limited strengthening.
Residual oxygen from milling may affect HCP precipitation kinetics.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis states that at least 6 hours of milling is required, but proposes that low hardness and absence of BCC in samples milled for less than 4 hours would falsify the hypothesis. That result would instead be consistent with the stated minimum-duration boundary.
The experiment specifies a 100 g Vickers load but expresses its hardness threshold as HV0.5, which denotes a 0.5 kgf (500 g) load; the load and hardness notation are inconsistent.
